title: Competitive Research Before NPD, Are We Innovating or Rebuilding What Already Exists?

Biradar Swapnil 1 min read · 20 hours ago -- Listen Share An engineering team identifies a problem and develops a solution. 6 months later, someone discovers that three competitors already sell comparable products at lower prices, with established distribution and validated field performance. The engineering work may still be excellent. The strategic research was not! Competitive analysis before NPD is not about copying competitors. It determines whether the proposed product creates enough differentiation to justify development. S tart with what customers can already buy How do existing products perform? What do they cost? Which materials and technologies are used? Where do customers complain? What patents protect critical solutions? Where are competitors over-engineered or underperforming? The objective is to locate the unresolved value gap . If competitors already meet performance requirements at ₹800, developing an equivalent product costing ₹1,100 provides little reason for customers to switch. But research may reveal something different: customers tolerate frequent maintenance because every available product has the same weakness. That weakness becomes an engineering opportunity. Benchmarking also prevents unnecessary innovation. Sometimes an established manufacturing architecture exists because decades of field experience have demonstrated that it is economically optimal. Reinventing it merely to appear innovative may increase risk without increasing customer value. Competitive research therefore connects market intelligence with engineering strategy. B efore committing to NPD, ask: What will this product do meaningfully better and will customers care enough to change suppliers or technologies because of it? Innovation is not creating something different. Commercial innovation is creating a difference that matters.
